criteria.evidence: "Each kind carries examples from more than one field (shop, clinic, bank), so the rules are not pulled toward one kind of product." / "Rules say what holds once the product is aligned; they never stop a write, because the model grows as plans are built in any order and a blocked write would lose work already found." / "Tracker Issue also stays there, because the tracker is where work is ordered, not part of the product model"

Acceptance: "Given the ontology on this branch, when check_ontology.py runs on it, then it passes with no errors." Rules and inputs/outputs are discrete bullets; What it does states the function's result ("The ontology ... defines every kind a plan uses"), not a user story.

"It is the one written agreement, at core/components/memory/standards/schemas/product-os/ontology.md, that a person and an agent both read to use the same words for the same things" (what); "a play cannot write or check a kind the ontology has not defined, so a plan that names an undefined kind cannot be trusted" (why); Out of scope hands the ready-check script to fn-724 and link checking/rename to fn-725 (edges).
